name: Simba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

tone_statements.citation: Mouguiama-Daouda, Patrick & Lolke J. van der Veen. 2005. B10-B30 : conglomérat phylogénétique ou produit d'une hybridation ? In Koen Bostoen & Jacky Maniacky (eds.), Studies in African Comparative Linguistics with Special Focus on Bantu and Mande (Collection Sciences humaines 169), 91-121. Tervuren: Royal Museum for Central Africa.
tone_statements.quote: Les systèmes tonals rencontrés en B30 diffèrent considérablement de ceux du B10. En Ts et Vi, se produit une propagation à droite des tons sous-jacents hauts suivant des règles bien précises, probablement sous la pression des langues du groupe B40, géographiquement proches, pour lesquelles on observe des « cas tonals » résultant de la propagation de tons hauts à partir de l'augment (cf. Blanchon 1998). On relève des systèmes tonals plus conservateurs dans des parlers comme Vo (Van der Veen 1991) et Hi (Rekanga 2001). Dans ce dernier, on observe certains changements tonals dus à l'augment.
tone_statements.translation: The tone systems found in B30 differ considerably from those of B10. In Tsogo and Viya there is rightward spreading of underlying high tones following precise rules, probably under pressure from the geographically close B40 languages, for which 'tonal cases' resulting from high-tone spreading from the augment are observed (cf. Blanchon 1998). More conservative tone systems are found in varieties such as Vove (Van der Veen 1991) and Himba (Rekanga 2001). In the latter, certain tonal changes due to the augment are observed.
tone_statements.locator: p. 5 of the DDL author version, section 2.2 'B30: aperçu des parlers et de leurs caractéristiques principales' (augment tonal realization: p. 17)

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 1999. Les Bantous eviya (Gabon-B30): langue et société traditionnelle. Note de synthèse HDR, Université Lumière-Lyon 2 (also HAL tel-05248957).
sources.note: Nothing on Himba stress or tone. Himba appears only in the B30 classification (proposed 'B34b ɣe-himba(ka)', 'Okani Nord' subgroup with Pinzi and Kande, pp. 6-7 of the text) and in the comparative noun-prefix table (p. 128 ff.); the phonology/tone discussion concerns Geviya.

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 1991. Étude comparée des parlers du groupe Okani (B 30, Gabon). Thèse de doctorat de 3e cycle, Université Lumière-Lyon 2 (dir. J.-M. Hombert; theses.fr NNT 1991LYO20013; Glottolog ref 156672, 427 pp.). Part I ch. VI 'Esquisse en vue de la description du ɣe-himba', pp. 233-242; Part II 1.1.3 'Les systèmes tonals' pp. 260-261; 1.2.3 'Tons' p. 283; 2.2.3 'Réflexes tonals' p. 336.
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. The Himba sketch (pp. 233-242, based on Hombert's 1988 ALGAB wordlist and Fontaney's 1987 notes) has phonology sections 2.1-2.5 (vowels, consonants, prefixes, syllable, base structure) but, unlike the Tsogo/Pove/Eviya sketches, no '2.6 Tons' section; p. 234 says the tones were not transcribed systematically, and p. 261 says the tonal study of P, K and H (H = ɣe-himba) remains to be done. The group is treated as tonal (Common Bantu tone schemes preserved in T, Vo, Vi; tonal reflexes regular, p. 336).

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 1988. 'Caractéristiques principales du groupe B 30 (Gabon)'. Pholia 3: 271-290 (Glottolog ref 64404).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Group overview; Himba (ɣe-himba, 'simba', ~400 speakers per Soret) documented only through an ALGAB list collected by J.-M. Hombert; comparative phonology/morphology/lexicon of B.30, tone marks given on group lexemes with 'tonalité incertaine' flagged (p. 278); no Himba-specific prosodic statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record simb1254 (JSON) and reference records 92848, 156672, 144634, 64404; Wikipedia 'Himba language' stub (no references); ELCat lang/4616 (no sources shown).
sources.note: Nothing; used only for bibliography and identity (alternate names Simba, Nsindak; Guthrie B.302).

sources.note: Section 2.2 (B30 overview): B30 tone systems differ considerably from B10; Tsogo and Viya show rightward spreading of underlying high tones (B40 influence, 'cas tonals'), whereas Vove and Himba (Hi, after Rekanga 2001) keep more conservative tone systems; in Himba certain tonal changes are caused by the augment, which has a segmental shape in classes 1, 9, 10 and probably a tonal realization in the other classes (p. 17). No tone inventory or count is given for Himba; the paper is second-hand on Himba tone (cites Rekanga).

sources.citation: Van der Veen, Lolke J. 2003. The B30 language group. In Derek Nurse & Gérard Philippson (eds.), The Bantu Languages (Routledge Language Family Series 4), 371-391. London & New York: Routledge.
sources.note: Chapter says no reliable tonal data exist for Northern B30 (Pinzi/Kande/Himba); the four noun melodies H, L, HL, LH are given for Tsogo, Vove, Viya only. Nothing on stress.

tone.quote: T, Vo and Vi have in common a tone system with basically four underlying melodies for the nouns (ie H, L, HL and LH) and two for the verbs (ie H and L). Tonal correspondances are about regular. No reliable tonal data are available for N-B30 so far.
tone.locator: section 2.2.2 'Tone systems', offprint p. 12 (chapter pp. 371-391 in the Routledge volume)

sources.note: The only full-length primary description of Himba (Glottolog's sole 'grammar' entry, 'full grammar'); a 577-page grammar almost certainly has a phonology chapter with a tonology section and is the place where any stress/accent or tone-vs-accent statement for Himba would be found; supersedes van der Veen's 10-page sketch.
